stories.title: Orangemen vow to stay at Drumcree until parade 'finished'
stories.summary: Orange Order members remain at Drumcree in Portadown with efforts set to intensify to find a political solution to a contentious parade which brought thousands of protesters on to the streets. The Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI) is maintaining a low-key presence near Drumcree Parish Church where a number of loyal order members stayed overnight in the expectation of completing their march through the Co Armagh town. This morning, five Orange Order members walked to the police line close to Drumcree Church. They were told by an officer that they were not permitted to proceed. But after a member of the public walked along the road, the five members removed their collarettes and walked again to the police line. After again being stopped, Portadown deputy district master Alastair Power asked the officer to confirm that a member of the public was allowed to walk down the road but his colleagues were not.

stories.title: Large police operation as protesters block parade route
stories.summary: A stand-off in Co Armagh continued this evening as hundreds of protesters blocked the route of an Orange Order parade. Thirty-five Orange men remain at Drumcree Church where they were due to start their march this morning. There is a large police operation on the Garvaghy Road and police occasionally used a loudspeaker to remind the crowd the protest is illegal. Protestors remain on the Garvaghy Road and Orange men stayed at Drumcree Church. There is no sign that police will move to clear the road. Orange men earlier said they should be allowed to proceed as permitted by the Northern Ireland Parades Commission. Neither Garvaghy residents nor Orange men are prepared to stand down.

stories.title: When true Gaza horror revealed 'it will shame the world'
stories.summary: The Taoiseach has said that when the true horrors of Gaza "are finally and fully revealed, it will shame the world". During his address to the United Nations General Assembly in New York, Micheál Martin said the international community has "failed Palestine" and criticised last year's Gaza peace plan, saying that it has not "changed the reality on the ground". "When the full truth of what has happened - what is still happening - in Gaza is finally known, when the evidence is gathered, when the testimonies are heard, when the true horrors are finally and fully revealed, it will shame the world," he said as the audience applauded. Mr Martin also hit out at attempts to make the prospect of a two-state solution "impossible". "It is the stated intent of the Prime Minister of Israel, who said clearly that 'we are going to fulfil our promise that there will be no Palestinian state. This place belongs to us,' as he permitted the E1 settlement development in East Jerusalem." The Taoiseach said that most countries have taken steps to push back against "the illegal and violent settler occupation of Palestinian land in the West Bank", but he said time is running out.

stories.title: China, US agree tariff cuts on $60 billion of goods
stories.summary: China and the United States have agreed to cut tariffs imposed on $60 billion worth of goods imported from each other, on an array of products ranging from US corn to cosmetics, and from Chinese household appliances to toys. Under the US-China Board of Trade, both countries have each recommended $30 billion of trade in non-sensitive goods for more favourable tariff treatment, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said in a statement on Sunday. For the United States, that was "unlocking improved market access" for about 30% of US exports to China, he said. The reciprocal tariff reduction as well as an extension of a trade truce were among the key takeaways from the second summit this year between President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump, hosted in Washington last week. One of two lists from the White House showed that China planned to trim duties on a variety of US agricultural goods including corn, wheat, sorghum, meat, dairy, vegetable oils and meals. It did not include soybeans. Beijing will also look to reduce levies on US fish and seafood, logs and wood products, cosmetics and medical devices.

stories.title: Iran insists on diplomatic solution as Trump rejects plan
stories.summary: Iran insisted that only diplomacy can solve its conflict with the United States and Israel after US President Donald Trump said he rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end fighting. "Our conditions are clear, and any move toward reopening the Strait of Hormuz is contingent on these conditions being met," Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi posted on social media. "Only a negotiated solution can get them out of this deadlock." Iran announced a peace proposal earlier this week at the UN General Assembly in New York, saying it had been transmitted to the Americans via Qatari mediators. Mr Trump said he rejected the plan and argued that desperation drives the Iranian push for an agreement on the key waterway. "They want to make a deal to open the Hormuz Strait immediately because they're losing so badly," Mr Trump told reporters at the White House.

stories.title: Israel captain: 'They hate us, we don't like them'
stories.summary: Israel captain Manor Solomon declared that his country was "ten times better" than Ireland following their Nations League tie in Debrecen, promising a "completely different game" when the sides meet again. The Boys in Green's early dominance decided the game in Nagyerdei Stadion with Troy Parrott, Adam Idah and Jack Moylan scoring goals in that period. The sides are due to meet again in Serbia on Sunday next, with Austria due in Dublin in between, but there are still some question marks remaining over that game in Backa Topola. The Irish players took a vote on Saturday morning to agree to play last night's game, with the majority voting in favour of doing so. At the same time, there was a significant minority opposed to playing, a figure that has not been confirmed by the FAI or manager Heimir Hallgrimsson, but has been reported to be either six or eight players. It remains to be seen whether further discussions amongst the players could see those numbers change.

stories.title: Hat-trick hero Nolan powers Mount Leinster to title
stories.summary: Chris Nolan was the Mount Leinster Rangers hero in the Carlow Senior Hurling Final at Netwatch Cullen Park on Saturday where he scored 3-06 for the holders as they retained their title in a pulsating finish. Rangers were quickly into their stride and while they fell behind to a Conor Kehoe free, Joe Dundon landed a great point from half-way to level matters. The champions in waiting threatened and only a smother defence prevented Nolan from getting in behind for what would surely have been a three-pointer. Rangers didn't have to wait too long and when Ted Joyce drew the penalty Nolan found the bottom left hand corner of the net. St Mullins depended on Kehoe’s accuracy from frees and were punished once again when Nolan looped around the St Mullins defence to shoot low and hard to the bottom right hand corner of the net. St Mullins did launch a long delivery into the Rangers small square which had the potential to cause problems but keeper, Dean Grennan, kept his eye on the dropping ball and cleared the danger. At the interval, Rangers led 2-07 to 0-08. Donagh Murphy landed an early Rangers point but a 33rd minute goal from Kehoe opened up the game. Unfortunately for the challengers, a looping shot from Nolan eluded the keeper and dipped under the crossbar for a three-pointer.

In midfield, Conor Coventry came in for Jason Knight, while Jack Moylan and Adam Idah started in place of Finn Azaz and Chiedozie Ogbene respectively. Jimmy Dunne is listed as third goalkeeper for Sunday's Nations League clash with Israel, following Gavin Bazunu's departure from the group.

stories.title: 11-man Australia hold on to defeat South Africa
stories.summary: Australia held on with 11 men in a dramatic finish to beat a second-string South Africa outfit 42-38 at Perth Stadium on Sunday and extend their unbeaten run to five games since new coach Les Kiss took over in late July. Skipper Harry Wilson, Ryan Lonergan, Joseph Suaalii and Hunter Paisami were all shown yellow cards in the last 10 minutes as the world champions cut a 25-point deficit down to four at the final whistle. Australia had looked to be cruising after centre Len Ikitau's double and tries from flyhalf Ben Donaldson, number eight Wilson and winger Max Jorgensen combined with 17 points from the boot of scrumhalf Ryan Lonergan gave them a 42-17 lead after 65 minutes. The last 10 minutes threatened to undo all their earlier good work but the Wallabies will move on to back-to-back tests against the All Blacks in October without a loss in six games, their best unbeaten run since 2017. "I'm so proud of the group," said Wilson. "Jeez, that was a crazy last 10 minutes, but that first 70 minutes, the way we played, we implemented our game-plan in exactly the way we wanted." South Africa coach Rassie Erasmus had made 13 changes to his line-up from the team which completed the gruelling 3-1 series victory over New Zealand earlier this month but stacked his bench with first-choice players as an insurance policy.

stories.title: 100 Buildings: Liberty Hall - the crystal tower of Eden Quay
stories.summary: Liberty Hall, home to the Services Industrial Professional and Technical Union (SIPTU), rose boldly into the Dublin skyline as the city's first high-rise and one of Ireland’s earliest purpose-built office buildings. Love it or loathe it, this striking tower has become an unmistakable and enduring landmark. At sixteen storeys and 60 metres tall, Liberty Hall arrived in a Dublin defined by a modest scale. Its slender form, perched on a 17.5-metre base, stands like a Modernist statement piece beside a low-slung auditorium. Designed between 1958 and 1961 by Desmond Rea O’Kelly (1923–2011), it claimed the title of Dublin’s tallest building upon its completion in 1965. Inside, it brought together a vibrant mix of spaces: offices, a reception lobby, a members’ cash office, and even a theatre, reflecting both function and ambition. Rea O’Kelly drew inspiration from Frank Lloyd Wright’s Johnson Wax Research Tower in Wisconsin, echoing its iconic tower-and-podium design. His vision took shape as a slim, square stack marked by alternating bands of light and dark, crowned with a distinctive green pagoda-style roof. Beneath its broad overhang, playful zig-zag mosaics shimmer in green, blue, and purple. The architect himself credited the nearby Custom House’s copper dome as the spark for this vivid flourish. Originally, white mosaic-clad concrete floors contrasted sharply with non-reflective glazing, giving the building a translucent, almost glowing quality. But Liberty Hall’s story is not without turbulence. In the winter of 1972, a car bomb outside the building shattered much of its glass, marking a turning point in its history. The rooftop viewing deck was permanently closed, and the building’s appearance was altered with windows being replaced with reflective, silver-coated glass to resist future blasts, while the colourful mosaics were sealed beneath protective coatings. Today, Liberty Hall endures, not as an overbearing giant, but as a slim, glass-clad sentinel linking Dublin’s past with its present. As Paddy Cahill so memorably described it, it remains ‘a souvenir of our first boom decade’.

stories.title: Nicole Scherzinger performs after suffering leg burn
stories.summary: Nicole Scherzinger performed with the Pussycat Dolls despite suffering a large burn to her leg after being scalded by boiling water shortly before a concert. "Nothing like boiling water falling on your leg an hour before your set, but the show must go on," Scherzinger wrote. Scherzinger went on to perform with bandmates Ashley Roberts and Kimberly Wyatt at Amsterdam’s Ziggo Dome on Sunday. The trio are due to bring their PCD Forever Tour to Dublin’s 3Arena on 5 October. They will first perform at Birmingham’s Utilita Arena on Tuesday, with further UK dates before the tour concludes at London’s O2 Arena on 13 October.

stories.title: Marco Pierre White on how to cook the perfect steak
stories.summary: Chef and restauranteur Marco Pierre White joined Brendan O'Connor to discuss his pivot from restaurants into curating a hotel, his ongoing quest to recreate his childhood and how to cook the perfect steak. Listen back above. Formerly known as the enfant terrible of cooking, as well as making history as the youngest chef ever to win three Michelin stars, Marco Pierre White is still a towering figure in the food industry. However, after handing back his stars and giving up cooking professionally, White has channelled his creative and romantic ideals into a new venture: a luxury hotel just outside of Bath in the UK. The chef acquired the Rudloe Hall Hotel in 2012 and reopened it as the Rudloe Arms in 2013, and has been slowly developing the property into his vision of opulence and luxury since. Speaking to O'Connor, White says "it's the most challenging job of my life". "When you build a restaurant, it’s a front room with a kitchen. When you’re building a 60-bedroom hotel and you’ve made that decision that every individual item has to be chosen, it’s a massive job." He explains that he collects furnishings and uses them to build "giant jigsaws" of design in the hotel, adding that, "what I did with food I now do with design". He mentions one room he's working on at the moment, for which he's bought artwork from Andy Warhol's Chairman Mao collection, which he's pairing with Mouseman furniture.

stories.title: Child spinal care commission of investigation recommended
stories.summary: A Government-backed scoping report into a series of children's hospital spina bifida and scoliosis controversies has confirmed a commission of investigation should take place to examine what happened but has stopped short of calls for a public tribunal-style inquiry. However, it is likely to focus on system issues rather than looking at individual cases, meaning it is likely the case of nine-year-old Harvey Morrison Sherratt who died in July last year after being on a waiting list since 2022 will not be specifically reviewed as an individual investigation. The scoping exercise has also recommended that the use of non-medical springs by one consultant at Temple Street Hospital between 2020 and 2022 will also be reviewed, with a focus on what Children's Health Ireland knew about the case. In addition, while the scoping exercise has said separate examinations should take place into spinal surgery and hip dysplasia issues during this period, these modules will not begin until separate ongoing current investigations conclude. The scoping exercise was overseen by senior counsel Remy Farrell and began its work in February this year. It was sent to families this evening, while separate briefings also took place for families and Oireachtas Health Committee members this afternoon.

stories.title: Possible lower carbon tax on home heating oil for Budget
stories.summary: The Minister for Public Expenditure has said that a lower rate of carbon tax on home heating oil is being considered for the Budget, but that Government "cannot insulate" the public from "every price change globally". Jack Chambers said there are trade-offs and choices with regards to the Budget, adding that "we have to ensure that we get the balance right". He said he has put reform and efficiencies and "wider productivity" at the centre of all the discussions he is having with ministers ahead of the Budget on 6 October. "It is about getting the balance right, between the short-term demands and the pressures of today." He said it was important to protect Ireland in a "period of significant risk within the global economy". The cost of a standard size of a household tank of oil has increased by 59% when compared to September of last year, due to the disruption of global oil supply with the ongoing war in Iran.

stories.title: Oil up 3% as US-Iran peace talks in stalemate
stories.summary: Brent crude oil rebounded more than 3% today after US President Donald Trump rejected a peace deal from Iran to resolve their conflict and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Brent futures rose $3.98, or 3.82%, to $108.30 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate crude was at $95.93 a barrel, up $3.52 or 3.81%. "Oil prices appeared to have jumped on the back of President Trump rejecting Iran's peace proposal," said Hamad Hussain," senior climate and commodities economist at Capital Economics. Iran announced a peace proposal last week at the UN General Assembly in New York, saying it had been transmitted to the Americans via Qatari mediators. Trump said on Saturday he rejected the plan, but told Axios in a phone interview on Sunday that he expected US negotiators to engage in more talks this week. "The rejection has reduced hopes of an immediate breakthrough, although diplomatic efforts have not ended," said Sugandha Sachdeva, the founder of SS WealthStreet, a New Delhi-based research firm. "For Brent futures, $120 a barrel remains the crucial resistance. As long as prices fail to sustain above it, a pullback remains possible, particularly if shipping improves or talks make progress."

stories.title: Pope Leo urges Church to face failings
stories.summary: Pope Leo has urged the Catholic Church to admit its own failings ⁠and heal "deep wounds" inflicted within its ranks, hours before he was set to meet victims of child abuse by priests in France. Leo, addressing crowds stretching out over a large field near the famed Catholic shrine in Lourdes, said the Church must have the courage to face its past but did not directly reference abuse scandals in France that sparked nationwide shock. "In order to heal the deep wounds, infidelities and painful errors that have occurred within (the Church), we must humbly place ourselves under the Lord's purifying gaze," the first US pope told an estimated 150,000 people gathered in the field on a sunlit day. Leo is on a whirlwind three-city, four-day visit to France, where he has again urged the world to reconsider the development of artificial intelligence. He drew around 800,000 people for an outdoor Mass on the Champs-Élysées in Paris yesterday. Local Church leaders are hoping he will help repair the Church's standing after a 2021 report found that some 330,000 French children had been abused by ‌Catholic clergy and lay leaders over seven decades. In an earlier, ⁠closed-door meeting with French bishops, Leo did directly refer to "the painful scourge of abuse committed against minors by members of the clergy," according to a Vatican-provided text.

stories.title: New Leinster Hurling Championship format nears completion
stories.summary: Leinster GAA will this week look to refine their proposal for a new senior inter-county hurling provincial championship of eight teams amid an extended structure. It is hoped that an agreed new format will be reviewed by counties and the Leinster GAA executive and presented before the media in early October. Former GAA president Nickey Brennan is chairing a special workgroup reviewing the structure of the Leinster Senior Hurling Championship to help developing counties achieve more meaningful access to elite competition The aim is to make the Leinster series as competitive as possible and lift developing teams who face steep challenges bridging the gap to higher terrain. From an early stage the plan was always set to consider expanding the current six-team round-robin format into an eight-team competition divided into groups. Factoring in the progress made by 2025 Joe McDonagh Cup champions Kildare – even though they experienced immediate relegation this season – was also a priority for the committee.

stories.title: Spillane eyeing quck return to the senior ranks with Tipp
stories.summary: Despite the disappointment of suffering relegation from the TG4 All-Ireland Senior Football Championship this year, Lucy Spillane is confident Tipperary can achieve an automatic return to the top-tier of ladies football in 2027. After losing out to provincial rivals Kerry and Kildare in the group stages of the Brendan Martin Cup, the Premier County found themselves facing into the All-Ireland SFC relegation play-offs. Following a four-point reversal to Tyrone at St Loman's, Mullingar on 4 July, Tipperary saw their seven-year stint in the competition coming to an end in the wake of a 0-15 to 1-80 loss at the hands of Waterford in Mallow GAA Sports Complex seven days later. While this was the fourth time in six seasons Tipp had been in a fight for survival, 2025 had seen them reaching the quarter-final stage of the All-Ireland race. Given how recently they made the last-eight of the Brendan Martin Cup, Spillane is optimistic her native county has what it takes to bounce back from a frustrating campaign. "We’ll definitely be pushing to get back up from intermediate. We are capable of it, although we did get relegated this year. It was a sad end to the year to go down," Spillane remarked. "We’ll try our best, we’re well capable of getting back up senior and performing at that level. We’ll just have to do it in intermediate now next year and then push on again." This won’t necessarily be new territory for Spillane as she previously featured at right corner-back (while still togging out for the Premier’s minor team) when Tipp were relegated to intermediate with a narrow defeat to Cavan in 2018.

stories.title: WSL wrap: Chelsea edge Arsenal, Spurs up to second
stories.summary: Chelsea beat London rivals Arsenal 1-0 at Stamford Bridge to move up to third in the Women's Super League. The Blues went ahead six minutes before half-time when the visitors were caught playing out from the back and Alyssa Thompson slotted in after Keira Walsh’s shot had been saved. The Gunners – who had drawn their last two WSL matches – improved in the second half, with Chloe Kelly’s angled drive blocked and Alessia Russo’s shot charged down, but the hosts saw out the closing stages for a third WSL win. Chelsea are level on 10 points with Tottenham, who had earlier thrashed Aston Villa 4-0, with Victoria Pelova scoring twice at the BetWright Stadium. Netherlands midfielder Pelova - signed after leaving Arsenal in the summer - broke the deadlock in the 54th minute and then fired in a second off the underside of the crossbar, taking her tally to four goals in two WSL games. Spurs - who thrashed promoted side Crystal Palace 7-0 last week - sealed a third WSL win of the new season after Caitlin Dijkstra headed in and Cathinka Tandberg added a fourth with two minutes left.

Accepting the award, she praised Parton as a storyteller whose songs were "so vivid and so rich". "I think that we were all very lucky to share this planet with Dolly Parton for a time," Swift told the audience. The tribute came on a historic night for Swift, who won three awards and became the most-awarded artist in VMA history. Her victories brought her career total to 33, moving her ahead of Beyoncé, with whom she had previously been tied on 30.

stories.title: Rise in prescription opioid use under public drug scheme
stories.summary: Approximately 1.5 million people, or around 30% of the population, are eligible for the General Medical Services (GMS) scheme, the country's main community drug scheme. Between 2018 and 2025, the State spent €316m on opioid prescriptions across the GMS and two other community drug schemes: the Long Term Illness (LTI) scheme and the Drugs Payment Scheme (DPS). Most of this expenditure, €271m, was through the GMS. The annual number of opioid prescriptions across the three schemes increased by 18% between 2018 and 2025. On average, more than two million prescriptions were recorded each year. Prescription opioid use has come into sharp focus in recent decades because of the US opioid epidemic, which has been the subject of several high-profile television series, books and podcasts. While Ireland has not experienced problems on the same scale, the use of prescription opioids under the main community drug scheme has increased in recent years. The aggregated data covers prescription opioids including oxycodone, codeine, fentanyl, morphine and tramadol. It includes information on costs, patient numbers and prescribing across the HSE’s 32 former Local Health Office areas (LHOs).

stories.title: Govt considering raising State pension by €7.50 per week
stories.summary: The Government is considering raising the weekly State pension by €7.50 as part of Budget 2027. The figure will bring the non-contributory State pension to €295.50 a week for anyone aged 66 to 79, and €305.50 for anyone aged 80 or over, as was reported in the Irish Independent this morning. While less than the €10 increase last year, Government sources have said any increase would likely need to take account of other competing requirements such as a potential bonus fuel allowance week to cope with the global energy crisis. No final decision has yet been made on the agreed pension increase level, or similar increases for social welfare payments, which have been repeatedly called for by Opposition parties and campaign groups in recent months. The Government leaders Taoiseach Micheál Martin, Tánaiste Simon Harris and Independent minister Seán Canney are due to hold their weekly meeting on Monday to iron out an agreed position, before Public Expenditure Minister Jack Chambers holds eleventh hour talks with various ministers next week.

stories.title: EU to delay methane emissions rules
stories.summary: The European Commission plans to postpone the European Union's landmark law to reduce methane emissions, a spokesperson has said today, following calls from governments including France and the United States to pause or roll back the policy. "The Commission plans to propose a postponement of the entry into force of the methane regulation," a European Commission spokesperson said, without specifying the length of the postponement. EU Energy Commissioner Dan Jorgensen said Brussels is exploring a one-year postponement of the law's rules for imported fuels, in an interview with Bloomberg News on Friday.

stories.title: Around 800,000 attend outdoor mass with Pope in Paris
stories.summary: Crowds stretched the length of the Avenue des Champs-Élysées in Paris, as Pope Leo XIV urged Catholics to find happiness in faith, not material things, at the biggest event of his visit to France, an outdoor Mass with an estimated 800,000 people. Chants of "Leo, Leo" and "Long live the Pope" echoed down the roughly 2km tree-lined boulevard, from the Place de la Concorde to the Arc de Triomphe, as people pressed against security barriers for a glimpse of Leo as he arrived in an open-top popemobile. The vehicle paused frequently as people waved white and yellow Vatican flags and Leo blessed people with disabilities, children and babies passed forward by volunteers. Attendees included Brigitte Macron, the French president's wife, far-right leader Marine Le Pen, who is leading in the polls ahead of next year's presidential election, Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu and Bernard Arnault, the billionaire chairman of French luxury group LVMH. Cheers rang out in the crowd as Leo thanked God in his sermon for the chance to visit France on a whirlwind four-day, three-city tour, during which he is seeking to repair the Church's standing after abuse scandals caused nationwide shock. The pope told Catholics that only their faith would provide true happiness.

stories.title: Snedeker: US team is 'going to be a problem in Ireland'
stories.summary: Victorious Presidents Cup captain Brandt Snedeker believes the United States team "is going to be a problem in Ireland" at next year's Ryder Cup. The 45-year-old received some criticism for his captaincy as they were staring at a first defeat on home soil after being dominated over the first three days at Medinah. However, his players turned things around after winning nine and a half points from the 12 singles matches to eventually prevail 17-13. Snedeker believes that offers hope – although the calibre of opposition did not compare with Luke Donald’s back-to-back winners – for the centenary edition of the Ryder Cup at Adare Manor in Limerick as they bid to win on foreign soil for the first time since 1993. "It doesn’t mean anything for me, it means more for USA golf," he said. "I think we’re all tired of this narrative that we don’t care about each other, that we don’t know how to play team golf. I think this proves it.
